entries.name: Lady Senara of Hindon (heiress/ward)
entries.dossier: Idnerth's only child (~19; mother long dead, no brother). Now Abisec's ward; hostile [Fate No, solar 482] — charged him with overturning God's judgment, certainty cracked when told the truth (incl. Achil's abduction, confirmed by Custennin) but not her hatred; rejects his wardship. On the road her father did NOT free her of the lie [Fate No]; Custennin will carry the truth after the burial. MATERNAL kin: royal-descended, the old line at EBBESBORNE, but headed by the wastrel LORD CADELL ('judged unfit'), who WON'T press for her [Fate will-press No, 34] — her hoped refuge is a hollow door; royal blood only makes her a richer marriage-prize (no land descends past the attainder [Fate No]). PARDONED by the King (482) — blood clean, attainder lifted; remains his sworn charge. Ulfius openly named the move: a marriage (Abisec×Senara) would unite deed-claim + blood-claim and end the quarrel — she still hates the man who broke her house. The marriage angle is live; she's hostile. She is a weapon either way — the Crown's marriage-pawn to 'clean' a Hindon grant, or a Morgan-shaped grievance pointed at the men who broke her house, Abisec foremost. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): Abisec offered her genuine CHOICE (back any path — convent, marriage, uncle's hall, Hindon, revenge on Gwythyr, even a marriage-knife) instead of disposing of her — cracked her guard [Honest 18 vs Suspicious 14, won partial]. Took her to Idnerth for the truth; Idnerth ExcNo'd [98] — recanted Gwythyr, named Abisec the wolf, counselled wed-and-ruin-from-within (the Morgan path is now her father's deathbed advice). She believes him → re-hardened. Abisec kept the oath with honor and withdrew [Honor success, rolled 1] — a hairline counter-crack. Marriage/agency offer open; she's hostile but conflicted. — Uther (482): her person/keeping stays Abisec's charge, but her HAND is the Crown's — the King warned Abisec off the marriage. She may ride to London for her father's end under guard. (Abisec's 'no one — the King's' to her holds true.) — Summer 482: watched Idnerth executed (unrepentant); then declined BOTH flight and her father's undermine-Abisec counsel [returns ExcYes; scheme No]. Came back composed, clean-handed, the old certainty spider-webbing. A genuine (if quiet) turn away from the Morgan path — open which way she breaks. — First court (482): she tested Abisec publicly; he passed (true justice, not her father's protect-the-useful-liar). Her first concession ('He'd have kept him... you are not what he told me'). The arc turns — hostility breaking toward something unnamed; not won, but no longer his enemy in her own mind. — Marriage-politics (Roderick, summer 482): Uther TORN on Abisec×Senara (aggrandizement vs. locking her loose blood-claim to a loyal man). Gettable as the King's gift on terms; a rival suitor (Gwythyr) reaching for her would tip Uther to allow it to Abisec instead. With Senara thawing, the match is quietly becoming viable on both the Crown and personal sides. — HINDON HOMECOMING, the keep wall (autumn 482): Abisec answered her honestly (justice done, but the master still at large), then took the homecoming bread & salt up to the rampart, gave her room, and asked how it had truly been for her. She did NOT fully open up [Fate Likely→No 54] — too proud, the wound too fresh — but gave the shape of it level & controlled ('the maids don't know what to call me — half think me a prisoner'; 'a fine thing to learn at nineteen the hall you were proud of was built on stolen silver'). The thaw HOLDS and warms a notch on one thing: Abisec's offer to recall her confessor **Father Custennin** landed ('the one face here that was never pretending') + 'thank you for asking; no one else has thought to.' Trust earned in inches, not poured out. She won't be rushed.

entries.name: Marriage / the dynasty (Adwen at Wilton; Senara)
entries.dossier: Heir urgency sharply up — Abisec nearly died at 23 with no heir; the line currently falls to brother Achil. Live prospects: SENARA of Hindon (would end the Hindon quarrel & unite the claims, but hostile); LADY NEST of Tisbury (genuine spark, door ajar — she wrote asking how he mends; her test is whether his danger is temporary); LADY GENERYS (Caradoc's daughter — old-guard alliance, may warm as Caradoc thaws; faith-tension); LADY ADWEN (Wilton widow, a £12 dower manor in hand, but a feud with her dead husbands' kin — 'come back when you've done your sums'). No heir yet. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): the Abisec×Senara route is now CROWN-BLOCKED — Uther reserved Senara's hand to himself and warned Abisec to his face off marrying her (don't unite the deed-claim with the blood-claim). So Senara is off the marriage table unless the King wills it. Live prospects narrow back to Nest (door ajar), Generys (warming as Caradoc thaws), Adwen (Wilton widow). Heir still urgent. — UPDATE (summer 482): Abisec's RISE reframes the whole market — a banneret-castellan is now a catch; Eluned: 'go choosing, not begging.' The field: NEST (door now OPEN + genuine liking — Eluned's pick); GENERYS (Caradoc's price met → could heal the old-guard feud; devout/faith-cool); ADWEN (called on, Courtesy 18 → receptive; a real partner + £12 manor, but the Goronwy-kin FEUD attached); new — LADY EILWEN of the western march (safe, clean dowry, alliance on the Gwythyr flank; green, unmet). Abisec's to choose. — RODERICK'S COUNSEL (Sarum, summer 482): as a TENANT-IN-CHIEF, Abisec's marriage is now semi-political — a knight's daughter Uther ignores, but a powerful match (a great honour / baron's heiress) needs the King's leave and will spook him (he denied the barony to keep Abisec dependent; same logic as blocking Senara). 'Marry small and stay free; marry big and wear the King's leash.' Roderick's lens: GENERYS mends the old guard (he'd welcome it); NEST safe & decent (Crown indifferent); ADWEN — don't buy a 2nd feud; EILWEN — useful flank but ropes him west into Summerland/Gwythyr's weather + Cadwal's troubles. Roderick will smooth a knight's-daughter match, OR make quiet inquiries for a higher Crown-friendly house IF Abisec wants to aim up (bringing Uther into it). Open question to weigh: what should the marriage DO — heir, peace, land, or power? — Roderick will QUIETLY LOOK AROUND for a higher Crown-friendly house (a season+ to bear fruit; a background process). And the SENARA option is reopened on new terms (Roderick's read): Uther isn't flatly against Abisec×Senara — he's TORN between (a) not wanting Abisec aggrandized (deed+blood = over-mighty) and (b) wanting the loose Ebbesborne blood-claim LOCKED to his loyal gate-holder rather than seized by a rival (Gwythyr). So the match is gettable — but only as the King's GIFT on the King's terms (humble petition, framed as Crown-security not self-gain, outliers stay Crown's, a tighter leash). THE LEVER that would tip Uther to YES: a rival (Gwythyr) reaching for Senara's hand. Combined with Senara's own thaw, the once-poison match is turning real from both ends — the most powerful but most Crown-entangled card in Abisec's hand. — (scene 8 denouement, 482): Abisec lightly asked the King about Senara's future; **Uther unmoved** [Fate Unlikely→No 70]: he keeps her hand RESERVED to the Crown (her Ebbesborne royal blood 'worth keeping, not spent in haste'), neither granting the Abisec match nor closing it — 'she's safe as your ward; leave it there.' The match stays Crown-blocked but not dead; Abisec's risen stock did NOT soften him (granting the heiress-ward mid-inquiry would look like self-dealing). Status quo: Senara a thawing ally & a deferred possibility, not a present prospect.

entries.name: Idris's death (the barrow; Gwenllian's unpaid debt)
entries.dossier: Sir Idris ap Cynan died in the storm of Hindon (482) taking a spear hauling Achil out; Abisec's First Aid failed (roll 18). Buried in a barrow on Salisbury Plain, his name in the county roll. On the road home Abisec offered to help bury him and pay respects, but Idris's mother GWENLLIAN (Cynan's widow, who lost her only son) rebuffed him cold [Fate No, 77] — 'lords always have friends to dig for them, and brothers who come back.' The debt to Idris's memory / to Gwenllian sits UNPAID.

entries.name: The second doubted lord (Idnerth's unproven charge: Gwythyr)
entries.dossier: Uther set his snare for TWO lords. Idnerth wore the Boar; the OTHER was never named at the time. Spring 482: the dying Idnerth NAMED him — GWYTHYR OF MERE — claiming they 'sounded each other' a year back and Gwythyr let him take the bait, now inheriting the valley with the King's eye fixed on the dead Boar. UNPROVEN (no seal, no proof). Roderick does NOT credit it [Fate No] and forbids speaking it without evidence — 'a knife with no handle.' A weapon against the rival if ever proven; poison to Abisec if wielded unproven. Open. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): Abisec REVEALED the Gwythyr naming to Senara (bending Roderick's keep-it-sheathed order). Confronted, IDNERTH PUBLICLY RECANTED it before Senara & Custennin ('I named no one; said it to soften the wolf') — the charge now actively DENIED by its own source. Abisec did NOT press it ('I'll not gainsay a man at his pass'), re-sheathing the lead. Net: Abisec still privately credits it (Idnerth named Gwythyr unbought in the cellar), but it's now discredited to Senara and any third party — murkier and harder than ever to wield. Still unproven. — Idnerth now DEAD (executed unrepentant, London, summer 482) — the only mouth that ever named Gwythyr is silenced and recanted; the lead is as cold as it gets, live only as Abisec's private conviction. (Meanwhile Gwythyr's men probe Hindon's western bounds.) — Note: Gwythyr reaching for Senara's hand (to revive the valley-claim through her Ebbesborne blood) is now a live danger — AND paradoxically the lever that would make Uther grant her to Abisec instead. Watch the careful man's marriage-moves.

entries.name: Old-guard friction (Caradoc, thawing)
entries.dossier: The old guard distrusts Abisec's fast royal-favoured rise. Caradoc's price was 'prove you'll last / hold a thing.' Then Abisec set his body against a baron in God's trial, took a lance through the chest, and lived — and now holds Hindon — and even Caradoc allows 'the boy has bottom.' Valour (and land) doing what charm couldn't. The Generys marriage-door may warm with the father.

entries.name: Hold & build Hindon's caput; Gwythyr's grudge
entries.dossier: RESOLVED in Abisec's favour (the hearing, 482): the King created Abisec Knight Banneret and granted him Hindon's CAPUT to hold for the Crown on his sworn perpetual-fealty vow; Gwythyr DENIED the valley; Senara pardoned. The full barony / Council seat NOT granted — the outliers stay in the King's hand, a thing to grow into by service. THE CAPUT: £55 (shell-keep castle DV 9/13/2 + a Mill + the wool market-town + home manors). THE OUTLIERS (NOT his): ~£95 in 8 parcels, escheat to the Crown, 'in question' only until Idnerth's vertict, then settled-forfeit — the King will likely break them up / feed a parcel to Gwythyr. STRATEGIC WEIGHT: the Hindon valley is the gate between Salisbury and Summerland (Cadwy's Mendip silver/lead Uther seized); Gwythyr holds Mere, the other gatepost. TO DO: harden the caput modestly from his own purse (~£50 plan — dammed town-moat, palisade + gatehouse round the wool-town, deep cistern, two towers); stout vs raiders/a rebel, useless vs a king's host (loyal initiative, not a power-base). Live successors: Gwythyr's grudge (the slighted, careful rival); the second-lord suspicion still unproven. Levers held: the storming + exposing the Boar; the King's favour; Roderick + Ulfius; the march. — UPDATE (spring 482, Abisec in seisin): the BOLT is UNDERWAY (£37) — wall + fortified gatehouse + wet moats around both town & keep + a drawbridge linking them (mill-stream dammed); core by raiding season, done by autumn. Household bound (Bledig sworn & retained under Mabli; Alun/Madog/Elad garrison; Sioned's infirmary — Hindon's healing name spreading). Toured town & villages [Courtesy 18: success] → wary folk WARMING (a lord who walls their homes beats a baron who taxed for his gilded hall). HOOK: a western hamlet's reeve confided that GWYTHYR'S men have been 'riding the bounds,' asking after an old boundary stone by the beck — the careful man testing the new neighbour's edges. ~£103 liquid left. — FIRST COURT held (summer 482): household oaths sworn publicly (Bledig seneschal, Mabli steward, garrison); mill-toll CUT for a year + hand-quern outlawed (relief + the lord's mill-right); the moved BOUNDARY STONE ordered restored to the true line & FENCED (a clear, lawful signal to Gwythyr's probe — the new neighbour counts his yards); a systematic wool-factor fraud exposed [ExcYes] & justly ruled (restitution+stocks+banishment, life spared at the commons' ask). Net: the valley's commons WON (a lord who asks, repays, and gives justice — loyalty no wall buys), the wool-staple's honest name restored. Gwythyr's grudge & border-probe still live.

entries.name: Stapleford pagan scandal (CLOSED)
entries.dossier: CLOSED (Plough Monday 481). Cynfael deflected; Iuan installed as a tolerant resident priest; the rite continues quietly. Watch: Cynfael will pounce on any future slip.

entries.name: Achil — RESCUED (CLOSED)
entries.dossier: Pulled from Hindon castle alive (spring 482) after a betrayal (the groom Tegid sold him, then was silenced by the Boar — boar-coin on his body confirmed Idnerth's hand). Survived two weeks by playing the useful leech. Changed by it — and by watching Idris die carrying him out; reforged in his healer-who-fights path. Heir restored. Crisis closed.

entries.name: The Boar Conspiracy (CLOSED)
entries.dossier: The central thread of 480–482, finished. ORIGIN (480): a royal courier on Salisbury Plain murdered and a sealed dispatch stolen by trained British-tongued men; Abisec ran them down, recovered a secret royal muster-order AND a snare — Uther binding trusted lords while secretly testing TWO doubted lords, one bearing a Boar badge; an informant inside Roderick's house had warned the Boar-lord early. CHAIN: Father Maucan (Vagon's chaplain, the informant, paid in boar-coin — captured, broken); Sir Cadeyrn (handler/grey-rider — captured, defiant); Baron Idnerth of Hindon, 'the Boar' (one of the two doubted lords). Trial-by-combat lost (Twelfth Night 481; Abisec maimed). But the Boar's abduction of Achil (482) handed Uther his pretext: a royal commission, the Salisbury host, and the STORM OF HINDON — Abisec planned and led it (deception + escalade), took Idnerth alive in single combat on the burning wall, and gave him to the King's justice rather than a knight's sword. Idnerth → Londinium cell & scaffold. COST: Sir Idris ap Cynan dead in the rescue. (Disposal → Hold-Hindon thread; the heir → Senara thread.) Loose ends: who else Master Gwyn's ledger named; the wider spy-network.

entries.name: The dangerous royal secret → ROYAL FAVOR (TURNED)
entries.dossier: TURNED (Twelfth Night eve audience). Uther himself noted Abisec had guessed the King's snare and kept silent about the King's business in front of the King — and PRIZED the discretion ('rarer than courage'). No longer a death-risk; a mark of favour. Abisec won the King's trust [opposed Honest 13 vs Suspicious 14 — won]; Uther counts him 'an honest instrument I can spend without watching my back,' honoured the Roderick chain, charged him as the Twelfth Night witness. Royal favour gained.

entries.name: Christmas board honour (480) (CLOSED)
entries.dossier: CLOSED — Roderick publicly seated Abisec among his favoured at the Christmas board (480).

entries.name: Vagon — granted, then reverted to Roderick (CLOSED)
entries.dossier: Salisbury's western watch facing Hindon (timber motte-and-bailey, DV 5/11/2). Abisec held it as castellan (Battle 18) + household knights (incl. Gwion) + ~10 sergeants/bowmen; ~£45 gross, ~£10/yr margin — power, not profit. REVERTS to Roderick's disposal (spring 482) now that Abisec holds the King's caput at Hindon and Stapleford stays the family seat.

entries.name: Christmas tournament (481) (RESOLVED)
entries.dossier: RESOLVED (Day 5, 481). Joust lost (unhorsed first course by Sir Petroc). Mêlée: Abisec's side won the field on his double charge (flank break [Battle 18] → pulled the eschille out and rear-charged [Battle 13] → enemy company shattered); then charged Brastias [opposed Lance 20 vs Sword 18 — Brastias won the pass but failed to unhorse him; Abisec rode it out, Horsemanship 15]. Brastias took the Champion's laurel; Abisec took the regard of Ulfius and the King (generalship noticed) + ~25 Glory. Redemption for the joust in the eyes that matter.

entries.name: The western march, bought — an innovative outside syndicate
entries.status: active(new) → largely RESOLVED; master overseas still faceless
entries.dossier: NEW THREAD (Turning Point on the altered homecoming, summer 482 — Thread NEW; Plot Points: Home Sweet Home / Sold! / Organizations In Conflict invoking Lady Eilwen). A clever OUTSIDE money-power [Faction goal: Inside Enemy Territory; tag: Innovative] has bought a foothold on the WESTERN MARCH around Sir Cadwal: bought up his debts, a mill & two fee-farms, and CONTRACTED Lady Eilwen's hand (Sold!) to their man — fast, by coin and contract, not charter and sword. The march is in uproar (Organizations In Conflict): Cadwal's house split, neighbour knights enraged that land & a bride changed hands for money. GM TRUTH [Fate No, 42]: it is NOT Gwythyr — a genuinely new power; Mabli reads it as a mercantile/financial operation, no Logres baron's style. WHO is behind it = unknown, to investigate. STAKES: Abisec's western flank infiltrated, a marriage prospect (Eilwen) taken, Hindon's own wool-economy a plausible next target. (Gwythyr at Mere will hate this incursion too — odd-bedfellow potential; the Crown, fresh off the Summerland accord, would mislike a destabilised march.) — INTEL (Mabli/Senara/town merchants, summer 482) [Mabli Stewardship 15: success]: PROFILE — a mobile, ruthless, OUTSIDE-FUNDED merchant-company [faction tags: Innovative, Mobile]; the coin is foreign (foreign weight to the silver, via cross-water channels — not valley/Sarum/London money), purse origin OUT of Logres, into the dark (deep mystery). METHOD — picks indebted minor march houses (more name than coin), buys the debt → the debt forces the marriage → the marriage takes the land; LAWFUL every step (Senara's read), which is why the sword-lords can't fight it ('you can't lance a contract'). AGENT (the loose thread to pull) — a brutally competitive merchant-factor who keeps HIRED MUSCLE; brusque, foreign coin, mobile (3 manors poorer in his wake). The wool-town fears it's next & asks if Abisec will stand for them. LEADS: pull the agent; follow the foreign coin to its source. — PLAN (summer 482): Abisec rates the DIRECT threat to Hindon LOW (the syndicate preys on the weak/indebted; Hindon is solvent, fortified, with a 6-knight eschille) but the strategic threat real (flank eroded, isolation, reputation) — and a useful counterweight to Gwythyr. Chosen response: INVESTIGATE + build a MARCH COALITION (be the protector the alarmed leaderless knights/barons lack — a defensible power-base under 'the King's peace'). Senara's steer: Cadwal is broken/useless; the rally-point is old BARON MEURIG (lost no ground, furious, the lesser houses follow him, knows every house's debts) — approach him as one who'll STAND FOR the march, not swallow it. — CADWAL'S TRUTH (summer 482) [Abisec Courtesy 18: success]: the method confirmed — his small honest debts were bought up at once into one fist, squeezed, then the agent offered 'mercy' = forgive all for Eilwen's hand + the manor. THE LEVER: it's all CONTINGENT ON THE DEBT — redeem Cadwal's debt (~£60) BEFORE the wedding and the marriage-contract collapses (the agent holds paper, not a wife). Agent due back to collect by HARVEST. Paying it = shatter the syndicate's claim here, free Eilwen, bind a grateful house on the weak flank, and PROVE to the watching march the syndicate can be beaten (coalition fuel) — at the cost of most of Abisec's ~£99 liquid. The deeper purse/master behind the agent remains unknown. — THE NUMBER IS A FORGERY (summer 482): Abisec smells the £60 — a small honest debt (~£12-15 over three lean years) bought up, then bred to threescore in one spring by interest-on-interest + INVENTED 'costs/fees' Cadwal never agreed to. [Fate Yes, 13: provable FRAUD, not mere lawful usury.] NEW & BETTER LEVER: don't pay the £60 — PROVE the fraud (needs Mabli + the debt-papers) → the debt dies, the contract dies, Eilwen walks free, and the syndicate stands exposed as FORGERS (a hanging matter; coalition fuel; lawful weapon). Cheaper than £60, far more dangerous to them — they won't take exposure quietly. THE GROOM [npcs roll]: an ambitious young FOREIGN merchant on the make (clothes 'like nothing worn this side of the water') — coin & foreign coin marrying into the noble blood to seize the manor; a clue to the syndicate's outland origin. NEXT: secure the ledger/evidence; Mabli builds the fraud case; choose the venue to break it (manor court / Roderick / the Crown); the agent returns by harvest. — MABLI'S VERDICT [Stewardship 15: CRITICAL] + THE MARCH'S STATE [Fate ExcNo, 88]: (1) WEAPON — Mabli proves the £60 forgery cold AND finds it's the SAME forging hand/method across many march houses' consolidated debts: a TEMPLATE, not a one-off. So the proof that frees Eilwen can VOID EVERY contract bought on a forged debt — the whole land-grab unmakeable at law (a court/Crown matter; forgery is a hanging crime). She's pulled a thread toward the forger's own hand (a lead toward the syndicate's centre). (2) BUT TOO LATE TO SAVE FORWARD — the syndicate moved fast (Mobile); most vulnerable Selwood houses are ALREADY fallen this spring (Maiden Bradley, Stourton, Kilmington — gone, wed off or turned out). Cadwal is near the last still saveable. PLAN INVERTS: not rescue-the-next-victim (coalition of sufferers mostly gone) but REVERSAL + EXPOSURE — break Cadwal's contract as the first domino, then use the systematic-forgery proof to unwind the purchases wholesale, restore the dispossessed, and rally them + the un-bought (MEURIG) behind the man who unmade the forgers. Venue TBD (shire court / Roderick / the Crown). Agent due by harvest. — INSIDE MAN FOUND (summer 482): a courtesy call on BARON TEWDWR OF WERESIDE [Awareness 13: success] reveals him as the syndicate's COMPROMISED NOBLE COVER — a debt-drowned royal-blooded wastrel they cooped (not devoured) to lend legitimacy & look away while they harvest his peers (foreign plate/coin in his hall; evasive on 'the newcomers'). A WINDOW into the syndicate + a LEVER (his ruinous secret), to work once Abisec's no longer his guest (Hospitality/Honor binds him now). RISK: Tewdwr may tip the syndicate to Abisec's poking. — MEURIG WON (summer 482) [Abisec Courtesy 18: success; honest pitch — forgery + asked his counsel]: the coalition SPINE secured. He'll lend weight + bring WITNESSES (wronged/dispossessed houses to swear the forged debts on relics) — turning the legal case into a march-wide reckoning. He does NOT suspect Wereside [Fate No] (Abisec's inside-man card stays private). CRITICAL STEER — THE SHERIFF IS SUSPECT [Fate No, 48]: Meurig distrusts the King's new shire-sheriff (untested, soft, Uther's centralizing appointee) and suspects he's BOUGHT — reasoning that ink-and-forgery could only eat a whole march 'lawfully,' deeds in order, if the officer who registers them is paid to look away. Implication (unproven, chilling): the syndicate's reach may run into the King's own administration — which makes it squarely a CROWN matter. PLAN: do NOT take the proof to the sheriff (it'd vanish + warn them); go OVER him to RODERICK (honest Count, his shire, Abisec's patron) → the KING. Free Cadwal as the first domino; muster Meurig's witnesses; carry the wholesale-forgery case up the ladder. Agent due by harvest. — THE KING'S COURT (midsummer 482): Abisec lodged the case (Roderick presenting) and FUMBLED the presentation [Courtesy: fumble, 20] — Uther's paranoia flipped the loyal play into 'who's been mastering my march behind my back, the thieves or you?' Recovery TIED [Honest 18 vs Suspicious 14 — no resolution]: his honesty stopped the fall but didn't dispel the suspicion. Then Abisec's SAVE [Courtesy 18: success, rolled 1] — instead of Roderick's surety, he asked the King to make NO ruling, only to SUMMON Cadwal + the foreign groom and judge for himself (the groom being Uther's would-be vassal — the King's own interest to vet him), framed as loyal duty. Uther embraced it (a paranoid test-loving King handed control). OUTCOME: the matter is now a CROWN MATTER — to be TRIED before the throne, Cadwal + the foreign groom summoned; Abisec to bring Mabli's forgery proof + Meurig's witnesses; the King's own eye (Intrigue 23) the blade. The syndicate's agent must answer a Crown summons or brand himself by fleeing. The voided lands will be Uther's to keep or grant. NEXT: marshal proof + witnesses for the royal trial; the sheriff & foreign-purse may surface under royal scrutiny; free Eilwen via the verdict. COST: Abisec's royal favor recovered from the brink but is now WATCHFUL, not easy. — THE CELL TAKEN (scene 7, midsummer 482): forewarned within two days of Abisec's audience (Meurig's read: the leak is the King's hall or the bought sheriff's rolls), the factor LIQUIDATED & RAN — dumped the Stourton mill, Kilmington fees, and Cadwal's debt-paper cheap to a Bristol buyer for portable silver, and let Eilwen's bride-contract LAPSE (Eilwen effectively freed pending the verdict). Abisec ran him down at a ford [chase CRITICAL] and took him ALIVE with the LEDGERS INTACT + the strongbox + 4 prisoners. The factor admitted he is only a CUTOUT for a principal ACROSS THE WATER whose name Abisec does NOT have, and offered to inform for his neck; Abisec REFUSED and delivers him WHOLE to Uther. STATE NOW: the Crown trial is imminent with defendant + physical proof + Meurig's witnesses converging at Sarum; the deep mystery (the foreign master overseas) PERSISTS; the bought sheriff unresolved; Gwythyr's spite a fresh black mark. — THE CROWN TRIAL WON (scene 8, midsummer 482): order = cold proof [Mabli Stewardship 15 → 18 FAIL: dry paper alone nudged Uther's suspicion] → the wronged men [Abisec Courtesy 13 → 1, strong success: a dozen relic-sworn dispossessed turned it, and the ledgers became corroboration] → the factor brought out BLIND [Q1 No: he won't lie into an unseen net, folds & confirms; Q2 No: a TRUE CUTOUT — cannot name the master]. VERDICT: forged debts void root & branch; bought lands restored to the turned-out; Eilwen free in law; factor + swords condemned; the foreign groom damned by his flight. The LOCAL land-grab is UNMADE and justice done. BUT the master across the water stays FACELESS ('a house behind three houses') — the deep mystery persists only as a cold documentary trail in the seized ledgers (a future hook for Mabli + cross-water inquiry). Down-weighted to a simmer.

entries.name: The factor's flight — the syndicate's march-cell breaks
entries.dossier: RESOLVED (scene 7, midsummer 482): both choke-point gambits FAILED [Meurig No 49 — men too scattered to watch the Severn in time; Gwythyr ExcNo 97 — refused the rider, let the factor cross Mere unhindered to spite Abisec]. Abisec ran him down alone [Horsemanship 15 −5 → check 10: CRITICAL] at a ford SHORT of the water, the silver-mules bogged at the crossing. The eschille routed 4 hired swords (2 down, 2 yielded); the factor surrendered hands-open. Cell BROKEN; ledgers seized INTACT before the river + a strongbox of foreign coin + 4 prisoners. Abisec REFUSED the factor's bargain and delivers him WHOLE to the King [Honor/Just]. Closed; the trial + the still-unknown foreign master carry forward on thread #14.

entries.name: The bought sheriff — rot in the King's new county system
entries.dossier: NEW THREAD (Crown trial, scene 8, midsummer 482): the trial exposed that the syndicate's forged deeds were registered 'lawfully' by Uther's new shire-sheriff (a 482 GPC appointee — 'sheriffs appointed across Logres'). Baron Meurig had named him bought; the King, hearing his own officer let a foreign power eat a march under the King's seal, said aloud 'someone in my own house was paid to look away' and will move on him. OPEN: is the sheriff a paid traitor or merely a fool the syndicate used?
